ideas.risks: This may only repackage the existing conditional lemma unless the explorer proves a new necessity statement or finds a real sufficient condition. It can also fail by excluding algorithms that use posterior-biased sampling, implicit optimization, or class structure without literal clean transcripts.
ideas.summary: Turn the solver's clean-transcript menu into a sharp dichotomy: either prove a black-box wrapper using the fixed weak source must, in some formal model, create a complete final classifier from total hidden-clean witness length K with inverse-polynomial discovery mass, or identify a non-transcript mechanism that escapes the p^{-K} bottleneck. Make the quantifiers exact: public data U, comparator c, p=Pr[Y=c(X)], witness length K, success q, advice/search cost, and validation independence.
ideas.title: Clean-Transcript Dichotomy
ideas.why_promising: This targets the current central bottleneck directly. A necessity theorem would explain why known boosting proofs stall; a counterexample mechanism would point to a new positive route.

ideas.risks: Constant additive oracle error may be too coarse for any convex-optimization implementation. The weak oracle optimizes over C, while the desired final class may be an exponentially large vote class without an efficient separation oracle.
ideas.summary: Revisit the da Cunha-style residual-free proof through implicit optimization rather than tuple and vote enumeration. Try to formulate the final vote selection as ERM or convex risk minimization over mixtures of realized weak outputs, using only polynomially many fresh population weak calls and finite-list validation at the end. Identify exactly whether the remaining exponential step is hidden-clean sample generation, final vote ERM, or clean-population generalization.
ideas.title: Implicit Vote Selector
ideas.why_promising: The semantic weak condition is already compatible with fixed beta; the gap is algorithmic. If the vote search can be replaced by an oracle-based or online-learning selector, the strongest positive near miss may become an atlas-polynomial theorem.

ideas.risks: Weighted bounded-distance decoding may already be hard in the weak regime, or approximate nearest-codeword hardness may disappear for improper hypotheses. Public handles, list decoding, validation, or code structure could also give a strong learner.
ideas.summary: Develop the code/decoding separation template concretely. Let concepts be codewords over coordinate domain X. Seek a represented code family with efficient distribution-free weighted bounded-distance decoding below radius gamma, but hard approximate nearest-codeword or RCN recovery at radius eta>gamma. The explorer should check whether strong agnostic improper learning under a uniform or weighted distribution would imply solving the hard decoding problem.
ideas.title: Weighted Decoding Separation
ideas.why_promising: It matches the hard band exactly: weak learning is useful only below gamma, while strong agnostic learning must solve instances at eta>gamma. A successful instantiation would give the serious negative route the run has been missing.

ideas.risks: The result may be too model-specific to say anything about the atlas edge. Low-OPT queries caused by public constants, artificial relabelings, empirical spikes, other concepts, or oracle handles may overwhelm the clean hidden-target accounting.
ideas.summary: Build a stopped public-filter oracle game around the adaptive smooth-filter lemma. Specify allowed query types, mass/smoothness conditions, canonical oracle replies, and exactly how returned hypotheses/evaluation access are charged to transcript information. Then prove that before the transcript accumulates enough information about a random target, no target-useful query crosses the hidden-noise threshold with nonnegligible probability.
ideas.title: Stopped Public-Filter Game
ideas.why_promising: This could convert the current toy information theorem into a precise black-box barrier, explaining why residual/filtering boosters cannot reliably enter the low-OPT regime from fixed slack alone.

ideas.risks: Sign-specific cells already refute global-correlation no-go statements, and richer class structure may create useful public cells. A clean theorem may require restrictive symmetry assumptions.
ideas.summary: Classify observable relabeling and filtering transformations generated from a current predictor g and the public sigma-field. Start with finite cells induced by observable variables such as Y, g(X), and previous predictions, then solve the minimax question: when does positive excess over c force any cell or relabeling to have c-error below gamma? Extend, if possible, to multi-step stopped processes with posterior-noise invariants.
ideas.title: Observable Relabeling Minimax
ideas.why_promising: It isolates a recurring failed proof step. Even a negative classification would prevent future residual-forcing attempts from relying on excess alone, while a positive special case could yield a new boosting primitive.

ideas.risks: Arbitrary improper learners can encode sample-dependent bits while preserving error, so a general positive regularization theorem may be false. Canonicalization may also require solving an intractable ERM problem over the output range.
ideas.summary: Investigate whether any fixed-slack improper learner can be transformed into a controlled-range or stable weak learner suitable for the da Cunha assumptions. Try sample splitting, repeated runs, validation pruning, output compression, or canonical tie-breaking. In parallel, construct weak learners that satisfy OPT+beta but force large VC or dual VC through irrelevant encoded bits, showing controlled range must be an extra assumption.
ideas.title: Weak-Learner Regularization
ideas.why_promising: This addresses a key conditional assumption in the positive route. A positive wrapper would unlock existing residual-free boosters; a negative construction would clarify why the atlas source alone is insufficient.
